newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt regrets U.S. veto in Boutros-Ghali vote.
newsitem.headline: Egypt regrets U.S. veto in Boutros-Ghali vote.

text.p: Egypt said it greatly regretted the U.S. veto of a second term for U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Tuesday and insisted on an African holding the post for the next five years.
A Foreign Ministry statement said the overwhelming support for the Egyptian diplomat was testimony to his achievements in office and the reforms he had made at the United Nations.
Fourteen of the 15 members of the U.N. Security Council voted in favour of Boutros-Ghali but the resolution recommending his reelection failed because of the U.S. veto.
The Foreign Ministry statement did not, however, say that Egypt would lobby the United States to change its mind. It hinted that another African candidate might be acceptable.

Expressing great regret at the result of the vote, the Foreign Ministry said: "The use of the veto by the United States obstructed the passage of the resolution although it won 14 out of 15 votes -- a matter which shows the reality of the overwhelming support for Dr Boutros-Ghali's nomination.

"This sweeping support is a testimony of appreciation for the achievements of Dr Boutros-Ghali in his first term, a term which saw many initiatives and achievements in the field of peacekeeping...and reforms which the international organisation has not seen in previous years.
"Egypt will insist that the sons of Africa continue the course of these achievements and reforms.

"It announces its confidence that Africa's right to a continuous second term in the position of secretary-general will be respected and it calls for consultations to continue with the Organisation of African Unity."
The statement thanked African states and other groups at the United Nations for opposing the U.S. veto.
